correctness.rationale: PASS: Maximal ternary order-four Kautz cycles correspond bijectively to Euler circuits in the overlap digraph of 12 proper length-three vertices and 24 proper length-four edges. Anchoring the unique edge 0101 removes rotation. Every complete Euler circuit determines one of 2^12 local binary in/out transition matchings; independently re-enumerated all 4096 systems using source-independent code, retained precisely 384 single-24-edge tours, checked all cyclic windows, and applied exact canonical rotation, reversal and six-symbol-permutation orbit computations: 24 reversal-fixed; 204 bracelets; 64 relabeling classes; 34 with reversal; 4 reflective relabeling classes. The general obstruction uses at most two fixed window positions of a cycle reflection: for odd k>=3 there are at least six proper palindromes of length k, contradiction; for even k>=4 and even q>=4, each of at least four length-(k-1) proper palindromes occurs q-1 odd times, forcing too many fixed positions. The finite census covers only q=3,k=4, while the parity necessity covers all q>=3,k>=3.
residual_risks: All-size obstruction is a necessary condition only; q odd and k even does not assert reflection-fixed cycles exist.
